name: NMHS Dialectical Behaviour Therapy Service (Osborne Community Mental Health)
who: Adults aged 18 to 65 living in the North Metropolitan catchment. The service page says the DBT group service is 'largely for people with borderline and emotional unstable personality disorder'.
referral: Self-referral, or a GP / other practitioner with your consent, using the NMHS electronic referral form. Email ReferralsStirlingCatchment@health.wa.gov.au or fax (08) 6457 8388.
location: Block H, Osborne Place, Osborne Park WA 6017. Mon to Fri, 8.30am to 4.30pm.
source: North Metropolitan Health Service: Community clinics

name: Fremantle Hospital community mental health (Alma Street)
who: Adults aged 18 to 65 in the South Metropolitan (Fremantle / Fiona Stanley) area.
referral: Single point of access for all mental health referrals and urgent assessment: (08) 9431 3555, 8am to 10pm, 7 days.
location: Outpatient clinic: Level 5, W Block, cnr Alma Street and Hampton Road, Fremantle. Mon to Fri, 8.30am to 4pm, (08) 9431 3400.
source: South Metropolitan Health Service: Community mental health services
note: The Australian BPD Foundation's WA list (dated Oct 2022) says DBT group programs run here. The SMHS page doesn't mention DBT, so ask when you call.

name: Peel Community Mental Health Service
who: Adults aged 18 to 64 in the Peel area.
referral: Not published on the main page. SMHS has a separate page for health professionals referring.
location: 50 Montsalvat Drive, Greenfields (relocated). Mon to Fri, 8.30am to 4.30pm.
source: South Metropolitan Health Service: Peel and Rockingham Kwinana
note: The BPD Foundation's WA list (Oct 2022) names this service among those with BPD programs. The SMHS page doesn't mention DBT, so ask when you call.

name: Rockingham Kwinana Mental Health Service
who: Adults aged 18 to 64 in the Rockingham Kwinana area.
referral: Not published on the main page. SMHS has a separate page for health professionals referring.
location: Cnr Clifton and Ameer Street, Rockingham. Mon to Fri, 8.30am to 4.30pm.
source: South Metropolitan Health Service: Peel and Rockingham Kwinana
note: The BPD Foundation's WA list (Oct 2022) says this service provides DBT group and individual work for people with BPD. The SMHS page doesn't mention DBT, so ask when you call.

name: Youth Axis (Youth Mental Health, NMHS)
who: Young people aged 16 to 24 in stable accommodation in the Perth metro area, who haven't had extensive specialist treatment, with features of emotionally unstable personality disorder (or ultra-high risk of psychosis). Time-limited: up to six months.
referral: Through the Youth Mental Health triage line, 1300 362 569 (Mon to Fri, 8.30am to 4.30pm), or the referral form emailed to youthmhtriage@health.wa.gov.au.
waitlist: The service says waitlist times vary. Call the triage officer to ask about current waits.
location: 32-34 Salvado Road, Wembley WA 6014.
source: North Metropolitan Health Service: Youth Mental Health

name: YouthLink (Youth Mental Health, NMHS)
who: Young people aged 13 to 24 with serious mental health problems who face big barriers to mainstream services, such as homelessness, transience, limited support, cultural barriers or previous bad experiences with services.
referral: Same triage as Youth Axis: 1300 362 569 or youthmhtriage@health.wa.gov.au.
waitlist: The service says waitlist times vary. Call triage to ask.
location: 223 James Street, Northbridge WA 6003. (08) 9227 4300.
source: North Metropolitan Health Service: Youth Mental Health

name: Lifeline WA DBTeen
who: Young people aged 14 to 18 who struggle to manage emotions and behaviour, together with a parent or adult carer they live with, who must attend all 12 sessions. Not for young people currently getting intensive hospital or community mental health care.
referral: Anyone can refer, including self-referral, a parent, a GP or a school, using the online form. Then there's an information session and an assessment.
waitlist: Not published. Intake is by semester: referrals are open for Semester 1 2027, with groups starting in the second week of February 2027.
location: Groups in Bentley, Landsdale, Yangebup, Rockingham and Shenton Park (evenings or Saturday mornings; may change).
source: Lifeline WA: DBTeen Groups

name: Perth Clinic: 12-week DBT Skills Program
who: The program page lists people diagnosed with BPD or BPD traits who can commit to the full 12 weeks. It also lists exclusions, including current alcohol or other substance use issues. Maximum 9 people per group.
referral: Only a Perth Clinic accredited doctor can refer to the group, not a psychologist. Your GP can refer you to an accredited psychiatrist first.
location: 21-29 Havelock Street, Perth WA 6005.
source: Perth Clinic: 12 Week DBT, and FAQs

name: Ramsay Clinic Hollywood: DBT Day Program
who: The clinic says it's for people with 'frequent and intense changes in their emotional state often leading to self-damaging behaviours'. One day a week for 13 weeks, with an optional 13-week advanced program after.
referral: GPs can refer directly. You don't need to have seen a psychiatrist first. A free intake assessment (about 1 hour) is done in person or by telehealth.
cost: The clinic says fees are usually fully covered by private health insurance or a DVA Gold Card, or you can self-fund. Self-funded price not published.
location: Hollywood Private Hospital, Monash Avenue, Nedlands WA 6009.
source: Ramsay Clinic Hollywood: Day Programs and GP day program booklet

name: Marian Centre: DBT day program and BPD inpatient care
who: The Marian Centre runs a 12-week day-patient DBT program for people diagnosed with BPD, plus inpatient care. Its day program page also lists a DBT-informed program (12 weeks weekly, or 6 weeks twice weekly).
referral: Admission must be under a psychiatrist with admitting rights at the Marian Centre. A GP or specialist refers you. Day-program dates: mrn.tlo@aurorahealth.com.au. Admissions team: 1800 540 388.
cost: You need private health insurance, DVA, WorkCover, or to self-fund. Out-of-pocket costs are confirmed by admissions; prices not published.
waitlist: The centre publishes an approximate wait of 1 to 6 weeks for day programs, depending on the program.
location: 187 Cambridge Street, Wembley WA 6016.
source: Marian Centre: BPD, Day Patient Programs and Referral Process

name: Abbotsford Private Hospital: DBT program
who: A voluntary private hospital for people over 16. Its DBT program is described as being for people 'struggling with emotional dysregulation'. It also runs addiction recovery groups.
referral: A GP or specialist referral, followed by an assessment with one of the hospital's psychiatrists. Assessments team: 0430 709 459. Email abbotsford@aurorahealth.com.au.
cost: You need private health insurance, DVA, WorkCover, or to self-fund. Out-of-pocket costs are confirmed by the hospital; prices not published.
location: 61-69 Cambridge Street, West Leederville WA 6007.
source: Abbotsford Private Hospital: Treatment and Programs, and Referral Process

name: MIFWA BPD Carer Support Group
who: Family members, carers and friends supporting someone with BPD or similar traits. Peer-facilitated by people in a caring role.
referral: Register your interest first. Registration includes a phone call with MIFWA's Carer Services team. No referral needed.
waitlist: Not published. Meets monthly, 5.30pm to 7pm, and alternates between Zoom and in person in West Leederville.
location: Online (Zoom) and West Leederville.
source: MIFWA: BPD Carer Support Group

name: Medicare Mental Health Centres (WA)
who: Adults. Free, walk-in support from mental health professionals and peer workers. Not a crisis service.
referral: No referral or appointment needed. You can also call the free Medicare Mental Health phone line on 1800 595 212.
location: Armadale (65A Church Ave), Gosnells (288 Corfield St), Midland (23 Old Great Northern Hwy), Mirrabooka (3/8 Sudbury Rd) and Northam (133 Fitzgerald St). Hours vary by centre.
source: WA Primary Health Alliance: Medicare Mental Health Centres

name: headspace (centres across WA, plus online chat)
who: Young people aged 12 to 25.
referral: Find your nearest centre on the headspace site. Online and phone support needs a free headspace account. Clinician chat runs 3pm to 10pm local time.
cost: Online chat is free. Centre costs not published here; check with your centre.
location: Centres across Perth and regional WA, plus online.
source: headspace: Find a centre, and Online & phone support

name: Here For You (WA support line)
who: Anyone in WA concerned about their own or someone else's mental health, alcohol or other drug challenges.
referral: Just call or email. No referral needed.
location: Statewide phone and online support. 7am to 10pm daily.
source: WA Mental Health Commission: Our Services

name: Alcohol and Drug Support Line
who: Anyone in WA seeking help for their own or someone else's alcohol or other drug use.
referral: Just call, 24/7. Email and live chat are also offered. Free call-back service.
location: Statewide phone, email and live chat.
source: WA Mental Health Commission (ADMHSS): Alcohol and Drug Support Line

name: Parent and Family Drug Support Line
who: Anyone concerned about someone else's alcohol or other drug use: a child of any age, partner, sibling, parent or friend.
referral: Just call, 24/7. From 8am to 10pm you can also ask to talk with a trained volunteer who has lived experience.
location: Statewide phone.
source: WA Mental Health Commission (ADMHSS): Parent and Family Drug Support Line

name: Community Alcohol and Drug Services (CADS)
who: People using alcohol or other drugs, plus their carers and families. Services include counselling, group programs, clinical psychology, withdrawal support and support for families.
referral: No referral needed. Self-refer by calling or visiting your nearest CADS.
location: Metro: Fremantle (08) 9430 5966, Rockingham (08) 9550 9200, Mandurah (08) 9581 4010, Thornlie (08) 9267 2400, Armadale (08) 9399 5344, Joondalup (08) 9301 3200, Innaloo (08) 9246 6767, Midland (08) 9274 7055. Regional services are listed on the source page.
source: WA Mental Health Commission: Community Alcohol and Drug Services

name: Next Step Drug and Alcohol Services: outpatients (East Perth)
who: Adults 18 and over (young people can use the Drug and Alcohol Youth Service). Services include shared care with other services, such as mental health, plus clinical psychology, counselling and assessment.
referral: Self-referral, or a referral from mental health services, a GP or other services.
location: 32 Moore Street, East Perth WA 6004.
source: WA Mental Health Commission: Next Step Outpatient Services, and Healthdirect listing

name: Your GP: mental health treatment plan
who: Usually the first step into most of the services on this page, including private psychiatrists and Medicare-subsidised psychology.
referral: Book a GP appointment, and say it's about your mental health so they can allow enough time. Healthdirect explains what a mental health treatment plan is.
cost: Depends on your GP (bulk-billed or gap fee)
location: Any GP.
source: Healthdirect: Mental health treatment plan
